title: Sheet Pan Maple Dijon Sausage and Veggies for Busy Weeknights
description: Make this easy sheet pan fall sausage dinner with sweet potatoes and Brussels sprouts. Fast, cheap, and cleanup is a breeze. Save money tonight!
story: By the time I dragged myself back to my little apartment kitchen last Tuesday, ordering Thai takeout for $25 felt way too easy to justify. Then I checked my banking app and remembered I'm trying to actually stick to a grocery budget this month. Aldi to the rescue! I grabbed a pack of chicken sausage, a couple of sweet potatoes, and some Brussels sprouts for less than $9 total. The first time I tested this sheet pan fall sausage combo, I crowded the pan too much and ended up with steamed, soggy veggies instead of that crispy caramelization we all want. Lesson learned: give everything some breathing room on the baking sheet! Tossed in a quick maple dijon glaze using pantry staples, this one-pan wonder saved my sanity and my wallet.
ingredients: 1 lb chicken sausage links (I use Trader Joe's sweet Italian or apple chicken sausage), sliced into rounds
2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into 1-inch cubes
1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
instructions: Step 1: Preheat your oven to 400°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper for easy cleanup.
Step 2: In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, kosher salt, black pepper, and garlic powder until smooth.

Step 3: Spread the diced sweet potatoes, halved Brussels sprouts, and sliced sausage evenly across the prepared sheet pan. Drizzle the maple dijon mixture right over everything and toss thoroughly with your hands to make sure every single piece is coated.
Step 4: Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender when poked with a fork and the edges of the Brussels sprouts are deeply golden and crispy.
proHack: Don't skip cutting your sweet potatoes into uniform 1-inch cubes. If some are huge and some are tiny, the small ones burn before the big ones actually soften through the middle!
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 3 days. To reheat, skip the microwave if you want that crisp texture back—throw them into a hot skillet with a tiny splash of olive oil for 4 minutes instead.

faqs.question: Can I use regular potatoes instead of sweet potatoes?
faqs.answer: Totally! Yukon gold or russet potatoes work great if that is what you already have in your pantry. Just cut them to the same size so they cook evenly.

faqs.question: How do I prevent my Brussels sprouts from burning?
faqs.answer: Make sure your baking sheet isn't overcrowded. If the veggies are piled on top of each other, they trap moisture and steam instead of roasting. Use two pans if you need extra room!
